questions.question: State six distinct steps or characteristics of the Samy worm attack and its impact, as described in the lecture.

marking_points.point: The worm injects JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It obtains the list of a user's heroes by performing a GET on a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It adds Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user who visits an infected user's page gets their profile infected with JavaScript and their friends list infected with Samy.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The worm eventually infected about one million MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The attack is a cross-site scripting attack because the JavaScript is dynamically injected into the web server via a user request and reflected from a third-party.
marking_points.quote: In a XSS attack, Javascript does not originate from a web server but is dynamically injected into it via a user request a following reﬂection from a third-party, a “cross-site”.

questions.question: Describe six distinct security mechanisms or features provided by Windows operating systems for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Windows uses tokens to store security credentials for subjects, providing a principal/subject mapping and additional security attributes.
marking_points.quote: Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: Windows implements discretionary access control lists (DACLs) to enable fine-grained access control of heterogeneous entities.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.quote: Standard access rights: common to most object types

marking_points.point: Windows includes Active Directory, an LDAP-like directory service for organizing users, groups, security credentials, and security policies.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are processes and threads, which are active entities in OS primitives.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.
